title: Deep Contextualized Word Representations
authors: M. Peters, M. Neumann, M. Iyyer, M. Gardner, C. Clark, K. Lee, L. Zettlemoyer
before: Static embeddings like word2vec and GloVe were the standard input layer.
problem: One vector per word cannot represent sense, syntax or reference, all of which depend on context.
breakthrough: Run a deep bidirectional LSTM language model and use its internal layers as the word representation.
why: It broke the static-embedding era and showed that a pretrained language model is a general-purpose feature extractor.
next: BERT replaced the LSTM with a Transformer encoder months later.
inherits: Contextual representations, now simply what a model's hidden states are.
